source.title: Mark 1:1
source.content: 1 This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
source.text: This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

verses.text: Este es el comienzo del evangelio de Jesucristo, el Hijo de Dios.

source.title: Mark 1:2
source.content: 2 As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”
source.text: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”

verses.text: Como está escrito en el profeta Isaías: «Mira, enviaré a Mi mensajero delante de Ti, quien preparará Tu camino».

source.title: Mark 1:3
source.content: 3 “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”
source.text: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”

verses.text: «Una voz de alguien que clama en el desierto: ‘Preparen el camino para el Señor, hagan sendas rectas para Él’».

source.title: Mark 1:4
source.content: 4 John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
source.text: John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

verses.text: Juan el Bautista apareció en el desierto, predicando un bautismo de arrepentimiento para el perdón de los pecados.

source.title: Mark 1:5
source.content: 5 People went out to him from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
source.text: People went out to him from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

verses.text: La gente salía a verlo de toda Jerusalén y de la zona rural de Judea. Confesando sus pecados, eran bautizados por él en el río Jordán.

source.title: Mark 1:6
source.content: 6 John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
source.text: John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

verses.text: Juan estaba vestido de pelo de camello, con un cinturón de cuero alrededor de la cintura. Su alimento eran langostas y miel silvestre.

source.title: Mark 1:7
source.content: 7 And he proclaimed: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
source.text: And he proclaimed: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

verses.text: Y proclamaba: «Después de mí vendrá Uno más poderoso que yo, ante quien no soy digno de agacharme y desatar las correas de Sus sandalias.

source.title: Mark 1:8
source.content: 8 I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
source.text: I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

verses.text: Yo los bautizo con agua, pero Él los bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».

source.title: Mark 1:9
source.content: 9 In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
source.text: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

verses.text: En aquellos días Jesús vino de Nazaret, en Galilea, y fue bautizado por Juan en el Jordán.

source.title: Mark 1:10
source.content: 10 As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.
source.text: As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.

verses.text: En cuanto Jesús salió del agua, vio que los cielos se abrían y que el Espíritu descendía sobre Él como una paloma.

source.title: Mark 1:11
source.content: 11 And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
source.text: And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”

verses.text: Y una voz vino del cielo: «Tú eres Mi Hijo amado; en Ti tengo complacencia».

source.title: Mark 1:12
source.content: 12 At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness,
source.text: At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness,

verses.text: De inmediato el Espíritu impulsó a Jesús al desierto,

source.title: Mark 1:13
source.content: 13 and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
source.text: and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.

verses.text: y estuvo allí durante cuarenta días, siendo tentado por Satanás. Estaba con los animales salvajes, y los ángeles le servían.

source.title: Mark 1:1
source.content: 1 I am going to tell you the good news about Jesus, the Messiah. He is the Son of God.
source.text: I am going to tell you the good news about Jesus, the Messiah. He is the Son of God.

verses.text: Voy a contarles las buenas noticias acerca de Jesús, el Mesías. Él es el Hijo de Dios.

source.title: Mark 1:2
source.content: 2 This story began as Isaiah, who spoke for God, wrote that it would: “Listen, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will make things ready for when you come.
source.text: This story began as Isaiah, who spoke for God, wrote that it would: “Listen, I am sending my messenger ahead of you. He will make things ready for when you come.

verses.text: Esta historia comenzó como Isaías, quien hablaba en nombre de Dios, había escrito que comenzaría: «Escucha, envío a mi mensajero delante de ti. Él dejará todo preparado para cuando vengas.

source.title: Mark 1:3
source.content: 3 In the desolate place, someone will be calling out {to the people}: ‘Prepare yourselves to receive the Lord! Make yourselves ready for when he comes!’”
source.text: In the desolate place, someone will be calling out {to the people}: ‘Prepare yourselves to receive the Lord! Make yourselves ready for when he comes!’”

verses.text: En el lugar desolado, alguien estará clamando {a la gente}: ‘¡Prepárense para recibir al Señor! ¡Estén listos para cuando él venga!’».

source.title: Mark 1:4
source.content: 4 Now there was a man whose name was John. He baptized people in a desolate area. He proclaimed that people should allow him to baptize them. That would show that they were going to stop doing what was wrong. That way, God would forgive their sins.
source.text: Now there was a man whose name was John. He baptized people in a desolate area. He proclaimed that people should allow him to baptize them. That would show that they were going to stop doing what was wrong. That way, God would forgive their sins.

verses.text: Había un hombre cuyo nombre era Juan. Él bautizaba a la gente en una zona desolada. Proclamaba que las personas debían permitirle bautizarlas. Eso mostraría que iban a dejar de hacer lo malo. De esa manera, Dios perdonaría sus pecados.

source.title: Mark 1:5
source.content: 5 Many people who lived in the region of Judea and many people who lived in the city of Jerusalem often went to listen to John. Many of these people agreed that they had sinned. Then, John baptized them in the Jordan River.
source.text: Many people who lived in the region of Judea and many people who lived in the city of Jerusalem often went to listen to John. Many of these people agreed that they had sinned. Then, John baptized them in the Jordan River.

verses.text: Muchas personas que vivían en la región de Judea y muchas que vivían en la ciudad de Jerusalén iban con frecuencia a escuchar a Juan. Muchas de estas personas reconocían que habían pecado. Entonces Juan las bautizaba en el río Jordán.

source.title: Mark 1:6
source.content: 6 John wore rough clothes that he made out of camel’s hair. He fastened around his waist a belt that he made from animal skin. He ate grasshoppers and honey that he found in that desolate area.
source.text: John wore rough clothes that he made out of camel’s hair. He fastened around his waist a belt that he made from animal skin. He ate grasshoppers and honey that he found in that desolate area.

verses.text: Juan vestía ropa áspera que hacía de pelo de camello. Se ajustaba alrededor de la cintura un cinturón que hacía de piel de animal. Comía saltamontes y miel que encontraba en aquella zona desolada.

source.title: Mark 1:7
source.content: 7 He often preached, “Soon you will see someone else who is greater than I am. It is not appropriate for me even to kneel down and help him take off his sandals.
source.text: He often preached, “Soon you will see someone else who is greater than I am. It is not appropriate for me even to kneel down and help him take off his sandals.

verses.text: A menudo predicaba: «Pronto verán a alguien más que es mayor que yo. Ni siquiera me corresponde arrodillarme y ayudarlo a quitarse las sandalias.

source.title: Mark 1:8
source.content: 8 I use water to baptize you. However, he will give you the Holy Spirit, which will be like baptizing you.”
source.text: I use water to baptize you. However, he will give you the Holy Spirit, which will be like baptizing you.”

verses.text: Yo uso agua para bautizarlos. Sin embargo, él les dará el Espíritu Santo, lo cual será como bautizarlos».

source.title: Mark 1:9
source.content: 9 Now while John was preaching and baptizing people, Jesus traveled from the town of Nazareth, which was in the region of Galilee. {He arrived where John was} and had John baptize him in the Jordan River.
source.text: Now while John was preaching and baptizing people, Jesus traveled from the town of Nazareth, which was in the region of Galilee. {He arrived where John was} and had John baptize him in the Jordan River.

verses.text: Mientras Juan predicaba y bautizaba a la gente, Jesús viajó desde el pueblo de Nazaret, que estaba en la región de Galilea. {Llegó a donde estaba Juan} e hizo que Juan lo bautizara en el río Jordán.

source.title: Mark 1:10
source.content: 10 As soon as John baptized him, Jesus waded out of the Jordan River. Then, he saw God opening the way from heaven. He saw that the Holy Spirit, who looked like a small bird, was descending {from heaven} to him.
source.text: As soon as John baptized him, Jesus waded out of the Jordan River. Then, he saw God opening the way from heaven. He saw that the Holy Spirit, who looked like a small bird, was descending {from heaven} to him.

verses.text: En cuanto Juan lo bautizó, Jesús salió del río Jordán caminando por el agua. Entonces vio a Dios abriendo el camino desde el cielo. Vio que el Espíritu Santo, que parecía un pájaro pequeño, descendía {del cielo} hacia él.

source.title: Mark 1:11
source.content: 11 Then God spoke from heaven, “You are my Son, the one whom I love dearly. What you do pleases me.”
source.text: Then God spoke from heaven, “You are my Son, the one whom I love dearly. What you do pleases me.”

verses.text: Entonces Dios habló desde el cielo: «Tú eres mi Hijo, a quien amo profundamente. Lo que haces me agrada».

source.title: Mark 1:12
source.content: 12 As soon as that happened, the Holy Spirit sent Jesus into a desolate area.
source.text: As soon as that happened, the Holy Spirit sent Jesus into a desolate area.

verses.text: En cuanto eso sucedió, el Espíritu Santo envió a Jesús a una zona desolada.

source.title: Mark 1:13
source.content: 13 Jesus stayed for 40 days in that desolate area with the animals that lived there. During that time, Satan tried to make Jesus sin. Also, angels took care of Jesus.
source.text: Jesus stayed for 40 days in that desolate area with the animals that lived there. During that time, Satan tried to make Jesus sin. Also, angels took care of Jesus.

verses.text: Jesús permaneció durante 40 días en aquella zona desolada con los animales que vivían allí. Durante ese tiempo, Satanás intentó hacer que Jesús pecara. Además, los ángeles cuidaban de Jesús.
